flawed_step: Lines 1341–1354: the definition of the low power abelian group uses e_k copies of every C_{p_i}, yet the proof claims this group has order n and acts freely and transitively on every n-element set.
counterexample: Take n=12=2^2·3^1, with k=2 and e_k=e_2=1. The displayed definition gives lowpower(12)=C_2⊕C_3, whose order is 6, not 12. Hence it cannot act freely and transitively on a 12-element set. The subsequent construction at lines 1402–1413 relies on its cardinality being n_i.
assessment_summary: The explicit n=12 instance refutes a concrete lemma required in the grouping construction. The likely intended inner bound was e_i rather than e_k, but the proof as written is invalid.
